platform_performance.reason: Latest strict 10 minute Pi 5 Labs target receipt at commit 0dd6660 validates .gvid, drops, memory, and interruption recovery at 19.98 fps median, which is acceptable as a conservative 20 fps Pi proxy for advancing camera integration. The entry remains blocked for firmware readiness because actual Mission 1 hardware still needs a 24 fps receipt. Follow-up probes on current and historical-doc commits do not reproduce the historical 24.93 fps result. Commit e16357f fixed the bench path so requested pixel format 4 reaches the encoder context; the corrected short direct .gvid probe is 19.85 fps median. A current-head tracked sweep at commit 03eaa4d records the reproducible direct .gvid baseline at 21.54 fps median and shows stripe64/deferred regressing to 18.52 fps median; its timing receipt points to Pass1 at 33.5 ms median, Pass2 at 11.6 ms median, and unpack at 20.6 ms mean. Polynomial-log, byte-exact u16 log-scratch, byte-exact prescale-2 fixed-shift, prefetch, LUT unroll, and decimated producer-ring probes were all slower than the LUT/default path. The best short direct-container near miss remains the scratch luma-pair shared-unpack candidate with stripe64/deferred rANS at 23.54 fps median and not committed. A later dirty-source channel0-to-channel3 luma-pair handoff probe was byte-identical locally but regressed on Pi to 12.05 fps median, confirming that cross-channel row handoff loses too much parallelism. If Mission 1 hardware misses 24 fps, the next speed path is deeper in-worker hot-path optimization, row-sharded shared-luma work, or a different capture-side algorithm.

hardened_wall_fps_probe.mode: native 12MP Mission 1 true-Bayer .gvid, hardened median+wall FPS gate
hardened_wall_fps_probe.reason: Valid .gvid, zero drops, interruption recovery, and Lexar SILVER PLUS storage-budget fit all pass, but strict production FPS now requires both median frame timing and whole-run wall throughput; this probe reaches 22.99 fps median and 22.40 fps wall against the 24 fps target.

native12_t236_boundary_probe.mode: native 12MP Mission 1 T236 quality-boundary profile, no REF content, real .gvid write isolation
native12_t236_boundary_probe.reason: T236 preserves the native 12MP quality/storage boundary and clears strict 24 fps when measured encode-only on the Pi. The remaining miss appears only after real .gvid write cost is included. The current-source 240-frame repeat records 44.235 ms total / 22.61 fps median with 22.21 fps wall throughput. The registered mission1_native12_t233 production profile already carries the faster FLL2 LL/pinning policy; its best repeat records 42.780 ms total / 23.38 fps median with 22.92 fps wall, while the latest settled repeat records 43.395 ms total / 23.04 fps median with 22.69 fps wall. The next production step is to reduce the production-profile tokenization/wall-time gap.
